subject: Clarifying operational evidence for LLM opt-out, prompt/response rights, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Ava Rodgers <ava@carecircle.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline + operational proof requests (LLM opt-out, prompt ownership)

Rafael —

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft. A few items legal and security have flagged that we need explicit confirmation and operational artifacts for before procurement will approve:

1) "No model improvement / no training" commitment: we need explicit language that interactions and prompt/responses will not be used to update, fine-tune, or otherwise improve models unless we opt in.
2) Prompt/response IP and export rights: confirm customer retains exclusive ownership of prompts and generated responses and that Redwood will not claim derivative rights.
3) Subprocessor transparency: we need a current inventory (names, regions, purpose) and which subprocessors have access to raw interaction data.
4) Evidence: SOC 2 + operations evidence for how non-learning is enforced (runbook, KV/prefix caching behavior, ephemeral TTLs, gating for adaptive training).
5) Data residency & KMS: confirm where data-at-rest will be stored for our pilot (we plan to use us-east-1) and whether we can use BYOK or an onshore KMS.

Attached is our initial redline for the DPA (CareCircle_DPA_redline_20280527.pdf). Can you provide the items above and any short attestation we can include in procurement? We’re trying to close the vendor review this week.

Appreciate a quick run-down and any operational stubs you can share.

—Ava
Ava Rodgers
Head of Platform Integrations
CareCircle Health

Attachments: CareCircle_DPA_redline_20280527.pdf (pdf)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Ava Rodgers <ava@carecircle.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + operational proof requests (LLM opt-out, prompt ownership)

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear list and for the redline. Looping in Kimberly from Legal so we can respond to the DPA text and provide formal language. High level answers below and we can attach the operational artifacts you requested:

1) No-model-improvement commitment:
- Redwood will commit, in the DPA, that CareCircle interactions will not be used to improve any general-purpose or proprietary model unless explicitly agreed in writing. For hosted API customers this is a contractual opt-in; for Dedicated/Private deployments the default is no-training without customer opt-in.

2) Prompt/response ownership:
- Customers retain all rights to prompts and generated outputs. Redwood will not assert derivative ownership or rights to sell or redistribute customer prompts/responses. We will add a concise clause in the DPA and the SOW to make this explicit.

3) Subprocessor inventory:
- We can provide an exportable CSV with current subprocessors, purpose, and region. See attached stub (subprocessor_inventory_20280530.csv). Note: this is the live inventory and we commit to 30-day notice for new subprocessors.

4) Operational evidence for non-learning:
- We will provide: (a) a short Non-Learning Attestation signed by our Head of Ops (attached as redwood-nonlearning-attestation-20280530.pdf), (b) an ops runbook excerpt describing capture controls (ephemeral KV TTL, prefix caching rules, and batching policies), and (c) SOC 2 Type II report summary pointers. For hosted plans we implement strict capture flags; for Dedicated/Private we can enforce capture=off at the tenant level.

5) Data residency & KMS:
- For your pilot in us-east-1 we can route storage to an S3 bucket in-region. For Private customers we support BYOK (customer-managed KMS). For Hosted customers we offer an onshore key-holder option and a contract addendum describing key custody and audit hooks.

Next steps: I’m attaching the inventory and our attestation PDF here for initial review. Kimberly, can you confirm whether the below wording would satisfy CareCircle’s redline on ownership and the no-improvement commitment? If legal wants a specific formulation I can run a short redline and return the DocuSign-ready DPA.

If helpful we can schedule a 30-min legal + ops call with Marissa (CS / onboarding) to run through the runbook evidence.

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

Attachments: redwood-nonlearning-attestation-20280530.pdf (pdf), subprocessor_inventory_20280530.csv (csv)

From: CareCircle Legal <legal@carecircle.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + operational proof requests (LLM opt-out, prompt ownership)

Rafael —

Thanks for the quick response and for the attachments. We reviewed the attestation and inventory at a high level; legal has the following asks before procurement signs off:

• Please provide the exact DPA clause language you intend to insert for the "no-model-improvement" commitment (we included a proposed phrasing in our redline but would prefer Redwood's suggested text).
• The subprocessor inventory is helpful — can you confirm which subprocessors (if any) have access to unredacted interaction transcripts vs. telemetry/metrics only? We need that distinction clearly marked.
• SOC 2: can you share a redacted SOC 2 report or an AICPA-provided letter? Summary links are okay but procurement requires a report stub.
• KMS custody: we prefer BYOK for production; confirm whether BYOK is available for a hosted pilot or whether we must move to Private. If hosted BYOK isn't feasible, please describe the onshore custodian workflow (audit logs, key rotation cadence).

We attached a redline with a few edits to make ownership and warranty language more explicit (see CareCircle_DPA_redline_20280527.pdf you received). Our timeline is tight — can you send proposed DPA language + SOC 2 stub by end of day tomorrow? Also cc: procurement@carecircle.com on your next note.

—CareCircle Legal
CareCircle Health

Attachments: CareCircle_DPA_redline_20280527.pdf (pdf)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Ava Rodgers <ava@carecircle.com>, CareCircle Legal <legal@carecircle.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + operational proof requests (LLM opt-out, prompt ownership)

Hi Ava / CareCircle team —

Thanks — quick update and artifacts attached per your asks:

1) Proposed DPA clause (text excerpt):
"Redwood will not use, access, or process Customer interactions for the purpose of improving, training, fine-tuning, or otherwise modifying any machine learning models, whether proprietary or third-party, without the Customer's prior written consent. All prompts and generated outputs produced in the course of Redwood's provision of services remain the exclusive property of the Customer. Redwood disclaims any rights to derivative works arising from Customer data."

(If legal prefers alternative phrasing we can run a formal redline.)

2) Subprocessors: attached CSV now indicates column "access_level" with values {transcripts_unredacted, telemetry_only, metadata}. In this export the only subprocessors with access to unredacted interaction transcripts are our on-prem transcription partner (US-based) and the logging aggregator used for debug snapshots (restricted by TTL and access controls). The majority are telemetry-only.

3) SOC 2: attached is a redacted SOC 2 Type II cover letter and an AICPA attestation link. Full report available under NDA — we can expedite a redacted copy for procurement.

4) KMS/BYOK: For the hosted pilot we offer an onshore custodian model (customer keys stored with our US-based key-custodian partner; we provide key-use audit logs and rotation records). BYOK is available for Dedicated/Private customers; we can pilot a BYOK flow for you if you prefer but it requires a short provisioning window.

Attachments provided: redwood-nonlearning-attestation-20280530.pdf (signed attestation), subprocessor_inventory_20280530.csv (with access_level column), redacted_SOC2_coverletter_20280530.pdf.

Next steps: Marissa (cc'd) will set up an ops runbook walkthrough and provide the runbook excerpt showing TTLs and capture=off enforcement for your engineering team. Kimberly will circulate a DPA redline with the clause inserted by EOD. If helpful we propose a 30-minute call (legal + ops) at your earliest availability — I can do 10:00-11:30 PT tomorrow.

Appreciate the rapid turnaround — we want to make sure this is procurement-ready.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193
